title: When the Colony Wakes
premise: Hazel Thackeray, sole navigator of the derelict freighter Vesper, has spent years maintaining a beacon whose original purpose was erased from the ship's records—along with most of the crew's memories. When a distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct since the Collapse, Hazel decodes it and learns the beacon is a tripwire: the backups sleeping in the hold are not spare copies of the crew but prisoners of a failed immortality experiment, and the signal is their kin calling them home. Racing a closing jump window to the relay at the edge of dead space, Hazel must choose between waking the sleepers—who may remember why the crew chose to forget—and preserving the fragile identity they've built from fragments. In the end, Hazel transmits the truth instead of the beacon's silence, wakes the sleepers at the relay, and accepts that survival means carrying memories that aren't only your own.
about_author: Hazel Ishikawa is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about signals that arrive too late. They live aboard a converted tugboat and insist the best stories are received, not invented.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Aboard the drifting Vesper, Hazel performs the ritual maintenance of the mysterious beacon while the ship's AI deflects every question about its origin. The backups in the hold hum in stasis, and Hazel's own memory gaps itch like scar tissue. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the comfort of routine curdling into suspicion that invisibility was chosen for Hazel, not by her.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, and Hazel reconstructs it using a dead grandmother's lullabies as a cipher key. Decoded, it names the sleepers by name—and names Hazel too, with a surname she's never used. The emotional beat is vertigo: identity cracking open as Hazel realizes the beacon was never a warning light but a cage alarm.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Open Window
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intercut with fragmentary logs from the erased crew. The Vesper burns hard for the edge-of-dead-space relay as the jump window narrows; the ship's AI finally confesses it was complicit in the forgetting. The sleepers begin stirring early, flooding Hazel with borrowed memories. The emotional beat is desperate momentum—grief and fury fused into velocity.

chapters.title: What Survives the Jump
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the relay, with seconds before the window closes, Hazel must transmit either silence or truth. She broadcasts the full record, wakes the sleepers, and meets the first of them: herself, or close enough. The emotional beat is costly reconciliation—Hazel chooses shared, imperfect memory over safe oblivion, and jumps through carrying everyone.
